suggested_actions: Increase coolant flow rate to secondary loop
rollback_steps: Restore turbine load to previous setpoint
Return coolant flow rate to normal baseline
risk_factors: Sensor may be reading a transient spike, not a sustained rise
Reducing turbine load can itself trigger a brief vibration transient
Coolant flow increase has previously masked a failing secondary pump rather than fixing it

suggested_actions: Lock out generator for physical inspection
rollback_steps: Cannot be rolled back automatically — requires manual inspection sign-off
risk_factors: Emergency shutdown carries its own restart risk on aging bearings
Vibration sensors near this unit have a known history of loose-mount false readings
A full shutdown halts production for the plant, not just the flagged unit

suggested_actions: Check for leaks in primary coolant line
rollback_steps: Deactivate backup coolant pump once primary is restored
risk_factors: Backup pump activation draws from a shared reserve tank used by two other systems
A slow pressure drop can also indicate sensor calibration drift, not a real leak
